  MINUTES
  VERNON CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  TUESDAY, APRIL 7, 2026
  COUNCIL CHAMBER, 4305 SANTA FE AVENUE

  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Lopez called the meeting to order at 9:01 a.m.

  FLAG SALUTE

  ROLL CALL

  PRESENT:
  Leticia Lopez, Mayor
  Melissa Ybarra, Mayor Pro Tem
  Jesus Rivera, Council Member
  Crystal Larios, Council Member

  ABSENT:
  Judith Merlo, Council Member

  STAFF PRESENT:
  Brian Saeki, City Administrator
  Mark Austin, Legal Counsel
  Genoveva Rocha, City Clerk
  Alice Hui, Finance Director/City Treasurer
  Veronica Petrosyan, Health and Environmental Control Deputy Director
  Su Tan, Human Resources Director
  Robert Sousa, Police Chief
  Dan Wall, Public Works Director-City Engineer
  Todd Dusenberry, Public Utilities General Manager

  APPROVAL OF THE AGENDA

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Ybarra moved and Council Member Larios seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. The question was called and the motion carried 4-0, Council
  Member Merlo absent

  PUBLIC COMMENT
  None.

  April 7, 2026

  PRESENTATIONS

  1.  Sexual Assault Awareness Month and Denim Day
  Recommendation:
  Proclaim April 2026 as “Sexual Assault Awareness Month” and April 29, 2026 as
  “Denim Day” in the City of Vernon in support of the Peace Over Violence sexual
  violence education campaign.

  City Clerk Rocha read the proclamation, and the City Council proclaimed April
  2026 as “Sexual Assault Awareness Month” and April 29, 2026, as “Denim Day” in
  the City of Vernon in support of the Peace Over Violence sexual violence education
  campaign.

  2.  Southeast Los Angeles Area (SELA) Cultural Center Presentation
  Recommendation:
  No action required by City Council. This is a presentation only.

  City Administrator Saeki introduced Esmeralda Garcia of the SELA Cultural Center,
  and she provided a presentation to the City Council.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  3.  New Regulations for the Discharge of Fats, Oils, And Grease to the City's
  Sewer System
  Recommendation: A. Conduct a Public Hearing; and B. Find that the proposed
  action is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review,
  because the adoption of the ordinance is not a “project” pursuant to California
  Code of Regulations, Title 14 section 15378(b)(2) as the ordinance is a general
  policy and procedure making activity; C. Introduce and conduct the first reading
  of Ordinance No. 1312, adding Chapter 13.25 to the Vernon Municipal Code (VMC)
  regulating the discharge of fats, oils, and grease (FOG) to the City's Sewer
  System; and D. Direct staff to schedule the second reading and adoption for the
  April 21, 2026, City Council meeting.

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report.

  Mayor Lopez opened the public hearing at 9:17 a.m. There being no speakers,
  Mayor Lopez closed the public hearing at 9:17 a.m.

  Mayor Lopez invited further Council questions. There being none, Mayor Lopez
  called for a motion.

  City Clerk Rocha read the title to Ordinance No. 1312 into the record.
 Docusign Envelope ID: 96105E64-C6C7-8E5B-826A-A9FEEB782B00

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 3 of 7
  April 7, 2026

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Ybarra moved and Council Member Rivera seconded a motion to
  approve recommendations A, B, C, and D. The question was called and the motion
  carried 4-0, Council Member Merlo absent.

  4.  Fiscal Year (FY) 2026-2027 General Fee Schedule
  Recommendation: A. Conduct a Public Hearing; and B. Adopt Resolution No.
  2026-013 authorizing and adopting the FY 2026-27 General Fee Schedule.

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report.

  Mayor Lopez opened the public hearing at 9:20 a.m. There being no speakers,
  Mayor Lopez closed the public hearing at 9:20 a.m.

  Mayor Lopez invited further Council questions. There being none, Mayor Lopez
  called for a motion.

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Ybarra moved and Council Member Larios seconded a motion to
  approve recommendations A and B. The question was called and the motion
  carried 4-0, Council Member Merlo absent.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Mayor Lopez invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Lopez, called for
  a motion.

  MOTION
  Mayor Pro Tem Ybarra moved and Council Member Rivera seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar and pull Item No. 10 for questions. The question
  was called and the motion carried 4-0, Council Member Merlo absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following items:
  5.  Meeting Minutes
  Recommendation: Approve the March 17, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting
  Minutes.
  6.  Claims Against the City
  Recommendation: Receive and file the claim submitted by Kemper Insurance as
  subrogee of Jackeling Mendoza Valle.
  7.  Operating Account Warrant Register
  Recommendation: Approve Operating Account Warrant Register No. 170, for the
  period of February 15, 2026 through February 28, 2026, totaling $9,177,841.11
  and consisting of ratification of electronic payments totaling $8,828,848.09 and
  ratification of the issuance of early checks totaling $348,993.02.
 Docusign Envelope ID: 96105E64-C6C7-8E5B-826A-A9FEEB782B00

  Regular City Council Meeting Minutes  Page 4 of 7
  April 7, 2026

  8.  Public Works Department Monthly Report
  Recommendation:
  Receive and file the February 2026 Building Report.
  9.  Report on Vehicle Purchase Approved by the City Administrator
  Recommendation: Receive and file a report on the City Administrator approved
  vehicle purchase of one 2026 Chevy Suburban Z71 from Chevrolet of Simi Valley
  for a total amount of $97,952.73.
  11.  Sidewalk Vending Regulations
  Recommendation:
  A. Find that the proposed action is exempt from the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Sections 15061(b)(3) and
  15378, as an action for which there is no possibility that the ordinance will have
  any significant effect on the environment; and
  B. Adopt Ordinance No. 1311 amending Chapter 12.10 (Sidewalk Vending) of Title
  12 (Streets, Sidewalks and Public Places) of the Vernon Municipal Code pertaining
  to the regulation of sidewalk vending.
  12.  Purchase Order with A-Best Industrial, Inc.
  Recommendation: A. Find that the proposed action is categorically exempt from
  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review, in accordance with CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15301, because the project consists of the maintenance, repair
  or minor alteration of existing facilities and equipment and involves negligible or no
  expansion of an existing use; and
  B. Approve and authorize the issuance of a Purchase Order with A-Best Industrial,
  Inc. for the purchase of gas regulators, for a total amount not-to-exceed
  $75,193.22.

  The following item was pulled from the Consent Calendar for individual consideration:

  10.  Memorandum of Understanding for the Maintenance and Operations of the
  John Anson Ford Park Infiltration Cistern Project
  Recommendation: Approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute the
  Memorandum of Understanding by and between the Cities of Bell, Bell Gardens,
  Commerce, Cudahy, Huntington Park, Maywood, and Vernon, in substantially the
  same form as submitted, for the maintenance and operations of the John Anson
  Ford Park Infiltration Cistern Project.

  In response to a question from Mayor Pro Tem Ybarra regarding Vernon’s higher
  cost share in comparison to other larger cities, Health and Environmental Control
  Deputy Director Petrosyan explained that the administrative fee was shared
  equally; however, the Pro-Rata cost share was based on the available square
  footage of land and since the City of Vernon possessed more industrial land than
  green space, the City had the second highest Pro-Rata share.

  In response to a question from Mayor Pro Tem Ybarra regarding the duration of
  the City’s participation, Health and Environmental Control Deputy Director
  Petrosyan explained funding for the operation and maintenance of the cistern is
 Docusign Envelope ID: 96105E64-C6C7-8E5B-826A-A9FEEB782B00

  April 7, 2026

  provided through Measure W and the seven cities would continue to participate in
  the regional project to maintain the cistern for as long as it is viable and operational.

  Mayor Pro Tem Ybarra moved and Council Member Larios seconded a motion to
  approve and authorize the City Administrator to execute the Memorandum of
  Understanding by and between the Cities of Bell, Bell Gardens, Commerce,
  Cudahy, Huntington Park, Maywood, and Vernon, in substantially the same form
  as submitted, for the maintenance and operations of the John Anson Ford Park
  Infiltration Cistern Project. The question was called and the motion carried 4-0,
  Council Member Merlo absent.

  NEW BUSINESS

  13.  Citywide Fringe Benefits Policy (Revisions to Holiday Section)
  Recommendation: Adopt Resolution No. 2026-014 adopting the Citywide Fringe
  Benefits Policy and repealing Resolution No. 2026-005.

  Human Resources Director Tan presented the staff report.

  Mayor Lopez invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Lopez called for
  a motion.

  MOTION
  Council Member Rivera moved and Council Member Larios seconded a motion to
  adopt Resolution No. 2026-014 adopting the Citywide Fringe Benefits Policy and
  repealing Resolution No. 2026-005. The question was called and the motion
  carried 4-0, Council Member Merlo absent.
  14.  Side Letters of Agreement with Various Bargaining Groups Regarding a
  Holiday Name Change
  Recommendation: A. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-015 approving Side Letter of
  Agreement No. 2 by and between the City of Vernon and the International
  Brotherhood of Electrical Workers, Local 47 (IBEW) regarding a holiday name
  change; B. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-016 approving Side Letter of Agreement
  No. 2 by and between the City of Vernon and the Teamsters Local Union 986
  (Teamsters) regarding a holiday name change; C. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-
  0017 approving Side Letter of Agreement No. 3 by and between the City of Vernon
  and the Vernon Police Management Association (VPMA) regarding a holiday name
  change; and D. Adopt Resolution No. 2026-0018 approving Side Letter of
  Agreement No. 3 by and between the City of Vernon and the Vernon Police
  Officers’ Benefit Association (VPOBA) regarding a holiday name change.
  Human Resources Director Tan presented the staff report.

  Mayor Lopez invited public comments. There being none, Mayor Lopez called for
  a motion.

  April 7, 2026

  MOTION
  Council Member Larios moved and Council Member Rivera seconded a motion to
  adopt recommendations A, B, C, and D. The question was called and motion
  carried 4-0, Council Member Merlo absent.
  ORAL REPORTS
  15.  City Administrator Reports on Activities and Other Announcements

  City Administrator Saeki reported that Moody’s upgraded the City of Vernon’s
  Utilities’ Revenue Bond Credit Ratings from A3 to Baa1, and revised the Utilities’
  outlook to stable. He indicated the well-deserved upgrade reflects the Utilities’
  strong financial performance in fiscal year 2025 and is important as it is indicative
  or fiscal stability and directly determines interest rates paid when borrowing funds
  for infrastructure projects. City Administrator Saeki also provided reminders related
  to the City’s General Municipal Election such as where the ballots could be
  dropped off and reminding residents to ensure mailed ballots are postmarked on
  the date mailed by requesting a manual postmark at the USPS retail counter, and
  he also stated the first Official Canvass would begin at 8:01p.m. at the City Council
  Chamber on April 14, 2026.

  16.  Council Reports on Activities (including AB 1234), Announcements, or
  Directives to Staff

  None.

  RECESS
  At 9:29 a.m., Mayor Lopez recessed the meeting to Closed Session.
  CLOSED SESSION
  17.  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation
  Initiation of Litigation
  Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4)
  Number of potential cases: 1
  RECONVENE
  At 9:42 a.m., Mayor Lopez adjourned the Closed Session and reconvened the
  regular meeting.
  CLOSED SESSION REPORT
  Legal Counsel Austin reported that the City Council met in Closed Session,
  discussed the item on the agenda, and took no reportable action.
